texts.label: text
texts.orig: On May 31, 2023, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (the 'Utility') and the Shasta County District Attorney's Office (the 'Shasta D.A.') reached an agreement pursuant to which they will file a civil stipulated judgment for the Shasta D.A. to dismiss with prejudice all criminal charges against the Utility in connection with the 2020 Zogg fire (the 'Zogg Stipulation'). Subject to the terms and conditions of the Zogg Stipulation, the Utility will pay a total of $50 million, which will not be recoverable through rates. On May 31, 2023, the Utility issued a press release regarding the Zogg Stipulation. A copy of this press release is attached hereto as Exhibit 99.1 and is incorporated by reference herein.
texts.text: On May 31, 2023, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (the 'Utility') and the Shasta County District Attorney's Office (the 'Shasta D.A.') reached an agreement pursuant to which they will file a civil stipulated judgment for the Shasta D.A. to dismiss with prejudice all criminal charges against the Utility in connection with the 2020 Zogg fire (the 'Zogg Stipulation'). Subject to the terms and conditions of the Zogg Stipulation, the Utility will pay a total of $50 million, which will not be recoverable through rates. On May 31, 2023, the Utility issued a press release regarding the Zogg Stipulation. A copy of this press release is attached hereto as Exhibit 99.1 and is incorporated by reference herein.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: PG&E and Shasta County District Attorney Reach Settlement to Further Enhance Wildfire Safety
texts.text: PG&E and Shasta County District Attorney Reach Settlement to Further Enhance Wildfire Safety

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Agreement Resolves Legal Proceeding in 2020 Zogg Fire
texts.text: Agreement Resolves Legal Proceeding in 2020 Zogg Fire

texts.label: text
texts.orig: OAKLAND, Calif.Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) announced today that it reached an agreement with the Shasta County District Attorney under which criminal charges arising from the 2020 Zogg Fire will be dismissed.
texts.text: OAKLAND, Calif.Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) announced today that it reached an agreement with the Shasta County District Attorney under which criminal charges arising from the 2020 Zogg Fire will be dismissed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In its settlement agreement with the District Attorney's Office, which is subject to court approval, PG&E has committed to continue several initiatives to further reduce the risk of wildfires, and to fund $45 million in contributions to numerous organizations dedicated to rebuilding and assisting Shasta County communities.
texts.text: In its settlement agreement with the District Attorney's Office, which is subject to court approval, PG&E has committed to continue several initiatives to further reduce the risk of wildfires, and to fund $45 million in contributions to numerous organizations dedicated to rebuilding and assisting Shasta County communities.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: PG&E already has settled civil claims with individuals, families, organizations and Shasta County to provide compensation for damages from the Zogg Fire, which CAL FIRE determined was caused by a tree falling on a PG&E powerline.
texts.text: PG&E already has settled civil claims with individuals, families, organizations and Shasta County to provide compensation for damages from the Zogg Fire, which CAL FIRE determined was caused by a tree falling on a PG&E powerline.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Today's agreement follows a Superior Court order dismissing over half of the 31 original criminal charges and a second, later, ruling tentatively dismissing all remaining felony charges. The court's tentative order noted there were multiple inspections in the area before the fire, that there was no evidence that PG&E's multiple inspections fell below the industry standard of care, and there also was no evidence that a risk involving the tree was visible before the fire.
texts.text: Today's agreement follows a Superior Court order dismissing over half of the 31 original criminal charges and a second, later, ruling tentatively dismissing all remaining felony charges. The court's tentative order noted there were multiple inspections in the area before the fire, that there was no evidence that PG&E's multiple inspections fell below the industry standard of care, and there also was no evidence that a risk involving the tree was visible before the fire.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 'The agreement reflects our continuing commitment to making it right and making it safe. We stand behind our thousands of trained and experienced coworkers and contractors working every day to keep Californians safe. We feel strongly that those good-faith judgments are not criminal,' said Patti Poppe, Chief Executive Officer of PG&E Corporation.
texts.text: 'The agreement reflects our continuing commitment to making it right and making it safe. We stand behind our thousands of trained and experienced coworkers and contractors working every day to keep Californians safe. We feel strongly that those good-faith judgments are not criminal,' said Patti Poppe, Chief Executive Officer of PG&E Corporation.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Poppe continued: 'I'm grateful that the Shasta County District Attorney has agreed to work with us to make her community safer, and we look forward to the relationship this agreement creates.'
texts.text: Poppe continued: 'I'm grateful that the Shasta County District Attorney has agreed to work with us to make her community safer, and we look forward to the relationship this agreement creates.'

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Highlights of commitments PG&E is making in Shasta County include:
texts.text: Highlights of commitments PG&E is making in Shasta County include:

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Wildfire Safety
texts.text: Wildfire Safety

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Local Vegetation Management : Implementing new systems for vegetation management work within High Fire-Risk Areas in Shasta County.
texts.text: Local Vegetation Management : Implementing new systems for vegetation management work within High Fire-Risk Areas in Shasta County.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Additional Wildfire Safety : Additional commitments relating to wildfire safety include installation of line sensor devices that improve the ability to locate faults on circuits, completing an aerial LiDAR survey, installation of new weather stations, and adding artificial intelligence-based technology to existing wildfire cameras.
texts.text: Additional Wildfire Safety : Additional commitments relating to wildfire safety include installation of line sensor devices that improve the ability to locate faults on circuits, completing an aerial LiDAR survey, installation of new weather stations, and adding artificial intelligence-based technology to existing wildfire cameras.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Quarterly Meetings: PG&E and the Shasta County District Attorney's Office will meet quarterly to discuss ongoing wildfire safety measures in Shasta County.
texts.text: Quarterly Meetings: PG&E and the Shasta County District Attorney's Office will meet quarterly to discuss ongoing wildfire safety measures in Shasta County.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ● Monitor: These commitments and others will be subject to a five-year monitorship in Shasta County. The Monitor will be independent of PG&E and will regularly report to the Shasta District Attorney on the company's progress.
texts.text: Monitor: These commitments and others will be subject to a five-year monitorship in Shasta County. The Monitor will be independent of PG&E and will regularly report to the Shasta District Attorney on the company's progress.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Payments to Community and Nonprofit Organizations
texts.text: Payments to Community and Nonprofit Organizations

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: As part of PG&E's commitment to work with local organizations and communities, most of the $45 million that PG&E will pay as part of the settlement will go to local fire departments and districts, law enforcement, and community and nonprofit organizations to rebuild and strengthen the communities affected by the Zogg Fire and to honor the victims.
texts.text: As part of PG&E's commitment to work with local organizations and communities, most of the $45 million that PG&E will pay as part of the settlement will go to local fire departments and districts, law enforcement, and community and nonprofit organizations to rebuild and strengthen the communities affected by the Zogg Fire and to honor the victims.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In addition, PG&E will pay a $5 million civil penalty to Shasta County. The financial commitments stipulated in the agreement total $50 million, and PG&E will not seek cost recovery from customers.
texts.text: In addition, PG&E will pay a $5 million civil penalty to Shasta County. The financial commitments stipulated in the agreement total $50 million, and PG&E will not seek cost recovery from customers.

texts.orig: PG&E's wildfire safety commitments across its service area are outlined in its 2023-2025 Wildfire Mitigation Plan, which the company submitted to the California Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety on March 27, 2023. More information about this plan and PG&E's work to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire is available here.
